newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil support at $24.90/bbl.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil support at $24.90/bbl.

text.p: Singapore front-month gas oil swaps were steady at midday in quiet Monday trading as the market received strong support at just under the $25.00 per barrel mark after this psychological level was breached on Friday, traders said.
"The market is well supported at $24.90. A lot of people came out to buy at this level late on Friday," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were last quoted at a wide $24.80-$25.00 per barrel range, largely unchanged from Friday.
Brokers said June traded down to a low of $24.85 per barrel on Friday before buyers emerged to prop the market up with more deals done at $24.90 and $24.91.
The market was untraded this morning.
Traders said market support was primarily due to expectations of crude run cuts by Singapore refiners and the sustained physical buying from a group of traders.

The three traders, who have bought more than 20 million barrels of gas oil since March 3, are not expected to go on a buying binge similar to that seen in late April when in one-day they bought a record 2.44 million barrels.
The traders' purchases are expected to be measured but enough to lend some support to the market to prevent a price collapse, industry sources said.
The traders on Friday bought five 150,000-barrel cargoes, three at $24.90 per barrel free-on-board Singapore basis for second half June lifting.
The deals at below the $25.00-support mark led to speculation among some that the market was poised to take a big price cut but others discounted this.
The sceptics pointed to potential demand from China and sustained support from the traders for their optimism.
But high middle distillate stocks which rose to an at least three-year high of 10.345 million barrels for the week ended May 21 led to arguments that the buying support might not be enough.
Barely two months ago, middle distillate stocks comprising jet fuel, kerosene and gas oil, were at an at least three-year low at 4.953 million barrels, the Singapore's Trade Development Board said.
June fuel oil was last quoted at $100.75/$101.75 per tonne, down about 25 cents from Friday, brokers said.
